title: Every Label Is Wrong
problem: Three closed boxes are labeled APPLES, ORANGES, and MIXED. One contains only apples, one only oranges, and one a mixture. Every label is wrong. You may draw one fruit from one box without looking inside. How can you determine all three contents?

hints.text: Choose the box whose incorrect label gives you the most information.
Because every label is wrong, the box labeled MIXED cannot actually be mixed.

solution.setup: Draw one fruit from the box labeled MIXED.
solution.reasoning: That box must be a single-fruit box because its label is wrong. If you draw an apple, it is the APPLES box. The box labeled ORANGES cannot be oranges and cannot be apples, so it must be MIXED; the remaining box labeled APPLES must be ORANGES. If you draw an orange, the same reasoning applies with apples and oranges exchanged.
solution.finalAnswer: Draw once from the box labeled MIXED, identify its single-fruit content, then assign the other two boxes by elimination.
solution.sanityCheck: Each final assignment contradicts every printed label and uses each of the three possible contents exactly once.

keyInsight: An explicitly false label is information; selecting the MIXED label collapses its possibilities to two pure contents, distinguishable with one draw.
recognitionCues: When every label is false, look for the label whose negation creates the strongest restriction.
commonMistakes: Drawing from a box labeled with a single fruit, which may produce that fruit whether the box is pure or mixed.
followUps: What changes if exactly one label, rather than every label, is correct?

source.notes: Original wording of a classic logic-puzzle family.

verification.notes: Both possible draws from the mislabeled MIXED box lead to a unique assignment.
